A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ObjEmbed. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ObjEmbed detection, referring-expression comprehension, retrieval, ablation, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds proposal-network experiments, distractor tests, and measured inference speeds.

M1.justification: The architecture, object/IoU tokens, global embeddings, matching procedure, and three-part training objective remain unchanged. Section 3.2 provides fuller loss specifications; the UPN experiments test an alternative proposal component without replacing the proposed default method.

E1.justification: The training-data mixture and detection, referring-expression comprehension, local retrieval, and global retrieval coverage remain unchanged. The added ILIAS experiment varies gallery distractor counts within the retained benchmark rather than introducing another task or domain.

E2.justification: v3 adds a component comparison between UPN and the default WeDetect-Uni proposal network in Table 10. Section 4.6 introduces throughput comparisons against Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B and Qwen3-VL-4B, which previously appeared in accuracy evaluations. The main benchmark comparator rosters are unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments vary WeDetect-Uni proposals across 50, 100, and 150, test UPN with 100 proposals, and evaluate ILIAS with 0, 5,000, and 10,000 distractors. FPS measurements are also introduced. Existing training settings and main benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds targeted checks of proposal-generator/count sensitivity (Table 10), retrieval sensitivity to distractors (Appendix C, Table 13), and inference efficiency (Section 4.6). Existing token, instruction, supervision, oracle-proposal, box-regression, and qualitative analyses remain intact.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores are retained. New results include the proposal sweeps and ILIAS mAP@50 at 10,000 distractors: ObjEmbed-4B scores 72.1/82.1 for T2I/I2I, versus 43.2/52.7 for Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B. Section 4.6 newly reports REC throughput of 4.0 versus 0.4 FPS for ObjEmbed-4B and Qwen3-VL-4B. These are additional evaluations, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly expands the already-described sigmoid focal objectives and image-level matching formulation. This supplies mathematical documentation of the existing losses, without introducing new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same object-oriented representation, versatility, and efficient-encoding contributions. The claims about 18 benchmarks and headline performance remain unchanged; the additions supply supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of robustness to proposal choice when recall is comparable, stability under additional distractors, and task-specific efficiency. Appendix B newly asserts minimal caption hallucination without adding an audit. The data-scaling and hard-negative limitations are retained, moving from Appendix D to Section 5.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly specifies focal-loss alpha=0.25 and gamma=2, learnable sigmoid scales/biases, separate parameters for regional and global objectives, and the global-batch loss construction. Section 4.6 explains reusable class-text embeddings and task-specific forward-pass requirements. These are documentation additions; the code link and existing training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to PrimitiveNet (Liu et al., 2024a) in the introduction and Panoptic Captioning (Lin et al., 2025) in Appendix B. The positioning relative to multimodal embedding models and open-vocabulary detectors remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision expands loss and benchmark explanations, adds an efficiency subsection, moves limitations into the main text, and adds acknowledgements. Author affiliations and contribution markers are updated. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 10 and 13. The training-data table moves and swaps numbering with the detection-results table, while several retained ablation tables reflow. The five figures retain their visual content, and the overall layout remains consistent.

improvement.justification: The added proposal and distractor tests strengthen empirical support, while fuller loss specifications improve reproducibility and timing measurements add evidence about efficiency. These gains are limited: ILIAS testing still stops far below five million distractors, timing conditions remain unspecified, and the new minimal-hallucination assertion lacks direct validation.
